posts.text:
Yadda yadda. Look, students voting at *home* would in many cases be better for Dems. Running up massive wins in college towns sucks Blue votes out of smaller places or red areas. 
I want people to vote in a way that links them to a community and ties them to consequences of their choices. /1

posts.text:
I feel about students voting on campus the same way I do about students engaging in college governance. Which is to say: I don't like people voting to alter towns and institutions where they are basically just passing through.

Now I have to go to work. Please keep down the whining and yelling.

posts.text: I didn't say what was legal, I'm talking about what's right. College towns love having kids vote, for many reasons, including that it's easier to borrow money when the town is full of kids who will never have to pay the bills. But it's dumb.
posts.summary: Criticizes college town student voting as fiscally irresponsible for municipalities

posts.text:
Yes, they should have to fly home or go by dog sled

or, you know, just vote absentee, which you can do by mail (and I assume in some places, online), as I did in college (and my daughter did in school a few years ago)

If you are defeated by the complexity of absentee voting, can't help you

Once again, people find the dumbest of the dumb arguments to make.
Vote where you live. You're a stay at home mom? That's where you live. 
Students who live for 9 months in a dorm and then go *home* should vote *at home*
